preview_en:
Kazakhstan begin life back in League C of the UEFA Nations League (UNL) with a difficult away game against the Faroe Islands .

Match News and Current Form

The Faroe Islands narrowly avoided relegation in the last UNL edition, winning only one of their six matches (D3, L2) to earn a third consecutive campaign in League C. They come into this fixture in excellent form though having won seven of their last ten games (L3), including victories against better-ranked nations Montenegro, Czech Republic and opponents here Kazakhstan. That upsurge in results should encourage head coach Eyðun Klakstein, whose rocky start to his permanent spell in charge - marked by three successive defeats - is now a distant memory. Three wins from their last four home matches (L1) also demonstrates their strength on their own turf as they begin their season in Tórshavn.

Kazakhstan are back in League C after spending just one cycle in League B, with their relegation from that level coming after they earned only one point in six games, failing to score even once. Immediate promotion requires a significant improvement in form, as the Hawks have won just once in their last six competitive matches (D2, L3), although that sequence includes an impressive 1-1 draw against top 10-ranked Belgium. New manager John van 't Schip’s primary focus could be addressing their away struggles, as Kazakhstan have lost 11 of their last 14 such games (W1, D2) and suffered four defeats in as many trips in this competition.

Head-to-Head History

The Faroe Islands have won three of the last five H2Hs (D1, L1), including a 1-0 friendly victory when these sides last met last November on neutral territory.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Just five of the Faroe Islands’ last 15 matches saw both teams score.

The Faroe Islands conceded exactly once in six of their last eight UNL games.

None of Kazakhstan’s last seven UNL matches saw both teams score.

Kazakhstan scored exactly once in five of their last seven games.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Four of Hanus Sørensen ’s five Faroe Islands goals have come at home, including their only strike against Latvia (1-1) in their last such UNL game. Maksim Samorodov ’s last four goals for Kazakhstan have arrived away from home or at a neutral venue, with all of those strikes coming before the hour mark.

The Faroe Islands have seemingly not suffered any injury withdrawals from their current squad, while Kazakhstan will be without Dastan Satpaev due to a hamstring problem.

Betting Analysis

The Faroe Islands are in better form than Kazakhstan, so backing a home win looks like a practical way to unlock value here.

Author: Sridhar Bhamidi
